study_identification.author_journal_year: Sun et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2025
study_identification.title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

study_characteristics.study_objective: To explore the heterogeneity of functional brain networks in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) using a normative modeling approach on resting-state fMRI data, identify subtypes of MDD based on deviation profiles, and characterize their cognitive correlates.

quality_checking_detail.answer: mean framewise displacement (FD) > 0.2 mm; visual inspection for imaging distortions; imaging signal lost in any ROI.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region. HBR allows for the imposition of a common prior distribution across multiple sites to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances, thus accommodating signal and noise variability in multisite data while preserving meaningful site-related variations.

response_variable.answer: degree centrality of brain functional networks

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex were mapped onto the degree centrality of brain functional networks. Site-related variability was minimized by using HBR.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) to model site effects, which is a method to handle nuisance structure.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: To minimize the impact of site-related variability on subsequent results, hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region (Fig. 1B). HBR allows for the imposition of a common prior distribution across multiple sites to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances, thus accommodating signal and noise variability in multisite data while preserving meaningful site-related variations (Bayer et al., 2022; Kia et al., 2020).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study performed 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy control (HC) dataset to evaluate the generalizability of the normative models.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: To evaluate the generalizability of the normative models, we first performed normative modeling on the HC using 10-fold cross-validation, and assessed the models using overall normalized mean squared error and mean squared log-loss.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not mention using an independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study mentions the lack of external validation as a limitation.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Secondly, although the sample size of this study was commendable, our findings have not yet been validated with external data from different populations.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: k-means clustering to identify subtypes. One-sample t-tests to assess mean deviations. Pearson correlation analyses between deviation values and HAMD scores. Two-sample t-tests to compare brain network deviations between subtypes. Partial least squares (PLS) regression analysis to explore the spatial correlation between cognitive functions and the observed deviations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Two distinct MDD subtypes were identified with opposing patterns of network topology between unimodal and transmodal networks.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Subtype 1 showed positive deviations in degree centrality in the limbic (LIM), frontoparietal (FPN), and default mode networks (DMN), but negative deviations in the visual (VIS) and sensorimotor networks (SMN). Subtype 2 demonstrated opposing patterns. These patterns were associated with different cognitive profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design, lack of external validation, incomplete clinical information, and group-level cognitive analysis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The findings offer a valuable reference for personalized diagnosis and treatment strategies for MDD.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used the Harvard-Oxford atlas with 96 regions. The AAL90 atlas was used for replication. The study used the Yeo 7 networks classification.
